title: CRISPY CHICKEN n' TOMATO, Kokushikan University Branch
subtitle: Bringing a well-known Korean fried chicken brand to a university cafeteria.
html:
Researching the market before approaching brands

Before introducing Korean fried chicken to Kokushikan University’s cafeteria, we first researched the market. Korean fried chicken coated in different sauces was popular in Japan at the time. My team and I identified two large brands and began discussing the possibility of bringing one onto campus.

Making the case for a first campus location

The franchise brand we approached had more than 300 locations at the time, and the monthly franchise fee was a substantial operating cost. In negotiations, we emphasized the story and visibility of a first university location, along with the experience it could offer the brand for potential future campus expansion.

This gave us a way to discuss the potential value of entering a university setting alongside the financial terms.

Training at the main location before the launch

Before the introduction, the bubble tea shop manager and I went to the brand’s main location for training. We studied cost analysis and product knowledge, giving me a clearer basis for considering product costs when discussing campus pricing and franchise terms.

Balancing student pricing with franchise costs

The hardest part was negotiating pricing with the university. Food sold in the cafeteria needed to be affordable for students, but reducing the selling price would compress the operating margin.

Using the first campus location as our negotiating point, we secured a more favorable monthly franchise fee and found a balance between student affordability and operating returns. The key was to negotiate the university’s pricing requirements, the brand’s expansion opportunity, and our operating costs together.
